services.name: Old files
services.testPosture: Unit and contract tests plus a recorded Windows run through the React control, the Tauri IPC boundary, the native Rust command and back into the rendered UI.
services.evidence: WINDOWS RUNTIME VERIFIED 2026-09-27T18:16:51Z on DESKTOP-FCJJB5O. React control click -> typed client -> Tauri IPC -> m04_old_files_complete -> real Windows measurement -> rendered result. Rendered: These files were not modified since 180 days ago. This machine does not reliably keep last-access timestamps, so "old" here does not mean "unused". This service is read-only. It never deletes, moves, or quarantines anything. Access time is system-managed, it is not applied to files. Windows reports disablelastaccess = 2, so last-access timestamps are not a reliable last-used signal. Rows fall back to modification time and are described as "not modified since". Measured from: fsutil, value as Windows reported it: 2. What this does and does not mean: The last-access policy is measured from fsutil and reported before the result, and the service refuses to call a file 'unused' when the machine does not track access time. The wording is 'not modified since', never 'not used since'. This is the exact distinction the module doc was written for, and it holds at runtime.

services.name: Windows permission dashboard
services.nameAr: لوحة التحكم في أذونات تطبيقات ويندوز
services.testPosture: Unit and contract tests plus a recorded Windows run through the React control, the Tauri IPC boundary, the native Rust command and back into the rendered UI.
services.evidence: WINDOWS RUNTIME VERIFIED 2026-09-26T22:58:00Z on DESKTOP-FCJJB5O. React control click -> typed client -> Tauri IPC -> m09_permission_dashboard -> real Windows measurement -> rendered result. Rendered: Real per-app camera, microphone and location consent entries were read; no permission was changed. Consent store present: yes. Application entries seen: 0. Allowed somewhere: 0. Changed any permission: no. Camera webcam 0/0/0/0: The consent store exists but lists no application. Microphone microphone 0/0/0/0: The consent store exists but lists no application. Location location 0/0/0/0: The consent store exists but lists no application. Extended location locationExtended 0/0/0/0: No consent store exists for this capability on this account. Providers consulted: CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore. What this does and does not mean: Provider: the per-user CapabilityAccessManager consent store. This account is a different one from the pre-reinstall machine, which recorded 2 webcam, 23 microphone and 3 location entries; zero here is a fresh measurement, not a regression. The service distinguishes a store that exists but lists no application from a capability that has no store at all.

services.evidence: WINDOWS RUNTIME VERIFIED 2026-09-26T22:55:56Z on DESKTOP-FCJJB5O. React control click -> typed client -> Tauri IPC -> m15_git_audit -> real Windows measurement -> rendered result. Rendered: Global Git configuration audit. Reads selected non-secret settings only. Tokens, passwords, and credential payloads are never collected. Version: git version 2.55.0.windows.3. Default branch: main. user.name: daynightae-cmyk. user.email: 293348050+daynightae-cmyk@users.noreply.github.com. core.autocrlf: true. Credential helper: -. Signing key: Not configured. Commit signing: Disabled. No Git configuration findings. The OperationResult envelope returned capabilityId m15_s03. services.name: Node & package-manager status
services.nameAr: حالة Node.js ومدراء الحزم (pnpm, npm, yarn, bun)
services.testPosture: Static contract evidence only; Windows runtime and E2E proof are not recorded.
services.evidence: Reads installed package managers plus the npm prefix and the PYTHONHOME, RUSTUP_HOME, CARGO_HOME and DOTNET_ROOT developer homes from the real environment, reporting an unset variable as unset. This service was previously published against `m15_git_audit`, which measures Git configuration, and has been re-bound to `m15_runtime_inspect`; the Rust envelope capability id was corrected in the same change. Windows runtime proof is still required.

services.name: Python & virtual environments
services.testPosture: No active native-handler test applicable.
services.evidence: No native command measures what this service names. Module 15 handlers used to be assigned by array position, which published the git, package-manager, port, repository, project, cache and HTTP commands against eight of the ten Module 15 services. The pairing is now explicit and these three services stay planned rather than being pointed at a command that measures something else. `m15.repositories.scan`, `m15.projects.audit`, `m15.caches.manage` and `m15.http.execute` are implemented and allowlisted but exposed by no catalog service, so their envelopes report `m15_unexposed` instead of borrowing another service identity.

services.name: Local port viewer
services.testPosture: Static contract evidence only; Windows runtime and E2E proof are not recorded.
services.evidence: Reads listening TCP and UDP endpoints from the Windows networking providers with the bound process name, command line and protected status. The native command is shared with M15-S09 and this service is the read-only listing mode; the Rust envelope derives its capability id from the request action so the two services cannot be confused. Nothing is terminated. Windows runtime proof is still required.

services.name: Process & port termination
services.testPosture: Static contract evidence only; Windows runtime and E2E proof are not recorded.
services.evidence: Shares `m15_ports_manage` with M15-S08 in its termination mode. Termination requires the literal token `STOP <pid>`, refuses protected processes and the application's own process, re-reads the port table to confirm the target is still listening, and reports whether taskkill.exe actually succeeded. No process is terminated without that token. Windows runtime proof is still required.
